A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and complete, including their equations, figures, tables and appendices. The authors, architecture, objectives and retained experiments establish that these are versions of the same work despite the changed title.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of NF-BC, NF-GCBC, NF-RLBC and NF-UGS across imitation learning, offline RL and goal-conditioned control, with additional numerical results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original evaluations and adds architectural and hyperparameter ablations in Tables 7–10, alongside timing comparisons in Figure 3b.

M1.justification: The coupling networks, generalized permutation flows, LayerNorm, objectives and inference procedures are retained. Noise injection, denoising and shared conditional/unconditional density estimation were already documented in v1. The new ablations test existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the four imitation-learning environments, 45 conditional imitation tasks, 30 offline RL tasks and three unsupervised ant-maze tasks. The added ablations reuse PushT, antmaze-large-navigate, scene-play and cube-single-play without introducing distinct task requirements.

E2.justification: v4 Figure 3a adds a BC comparison on PushT, absent from v1 Figure 3. BeT, VQ-BeT and both diffusion-policy variants remain. Comparator membership in the conditional imitation, offline RL and unsupervised exploration comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce controlled sweeps over NF depth, coupling width and noise, plus component-removal controls for NF-GCBC. Figure 3b also introduces inference and training time as comparison metrics, although measurement procedures are unspecified. The original evaluation procedures and Appendix A settings are retained.

E4.justification: v1 contains no corresponding ablation program. v4 Appendix D and Tables 7–10 test capacity and noise sensitivity on PushT and isolate permutation flows, LayerNorm and denoising on three conditional imitation environments. These provide substantial new evidence about component necessity and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five seeds, standard deviations by default and standard errors for NF-BC in the imitation-learning plot. The new checklist repeats these conventions without introducing additional runs, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new ablation tables supply point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v4 adds timing results, BC's 0.65 PushT score and the ablation results, including NaN at zero noise and cube-single-play dropping from 0.795 to zero without permutation flows or LayerNorm. v1 Tables 7–8 are retained exactly as v4 Tables 11–12. Shared Figure 3 means are rescaled equivalents, but uncertainty widths change on a common normalized scale. Its new top-two claim conflicts with the Ant and Kitchen bars.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, occupancy formulation and coupling-layer derivations remain unchanged. Corrections such as writing the prior as p0(z) instead of p0(x) clarify notation without changing mathematical reasoning, assumptions or formal results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims that NFs provide expressive, simple models for policies, value functions and occupancy densities across the same RL settings. The headline contribution claims, including the 82-task evaluation and offline RL performance claims, remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Table 10 newly interprets the architectural components as crucial to performance. Section 6.1 broadens the practical simplicity argument to emphasize inference speed and end-to-end optimization. The existing likelihood-based explanation, action-gradient rationale, exploration interpretation and architectural limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Figure 3b adds explicit inference/training timings and an objective-count comparison, but omits timing conditions. Appendix A's implementation settings, hardware and training-duration disclosures remain unchanged. The repository linked in v4's opening footnote was already linked in v1 Section 5.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for JAX, PyTorch and Tarasov et al.'s ReBRAC work, giving the already evaluated ReBRAC baseline its source citation. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to prior NF architectures and other probabilistic models remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from RL to Continuous Control, with localized wording, terminology and caption edits. v4 adds ablation, societal-impact and checklist sections and moves the hyperparameter catalogue from Appendix D to E. Most main-text prose and the narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is substantially redesigned from performance-versus-simplicity scatterplots and a parameter plot into four bar charts and a timing/parameters/architecture/objectives table incorporating material from the former Figure 4. Three task axes change scale. Four ablation tables are added; the other principal plots and existing appendix tables are largely retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new ablations address v1's missing evidence about component necessity and hyperparameter sensitivity, strengthening the design rationale on selected tasks. The net gain is limited by missing ablation uncertainty and timing procedures, plus unsupported top-two wording and unexplained uncertainty changes in the redesigned Figure 3. The core benchmark evidence and conclusions otherwise remain intact.
